title: He was ready to start a war… and God said, “Stop.”
paragraphs: He was ready to start a war… and God said, “Stop.”
Pause.
Because this is where most of us fail.
You think the real danger is losing.
No.
The real danger is winning a fight God never told you to fight.

Rehoboam had the numbers.
180,000 warriors.
Steel sharpened.
Blood pressure rising.

This wasn’t just strategy.
This was pride… dressed as justice.
And maybe that’s where this hits you.
Because not all your battles are holy.
Some of them are just your ego… screaming.
Here’s the tension:

You feel justified.
You feel wronged.
You feel like silence means weakness.

So you prepare your words.
Sharpen your response.
Load your emotions like weapons.
You’re ready.
Ready to “set things right.”
But what if heaven is not backing your fight?
What if God is not in your anger?
What if you’re about to destroy something God actually allowed?
Enter a man most people skip.
Shemaiah.

No army.
No rank.
No applause.
Just a message.

“You shall not go up or fight against your relatives… for this thing is from Me.”
— 1 Kings 12:24
Let that sink in.
“This thing… is from Me.”
God was saying:
“This conflict you hate… I allowed it.”
And that changes everything.
Some scholars interpret this as God’s judgment unfolding through the division of the kingdom.
Others see it as a moment where God restrains greater destruction.
But both agree on this:
God was in control—even in the chaos.
And He was not giving permission to fight.
This is where pride gets exposed.

Because pride doesn’t ask,
“Is God in this?”

Pride asks,
“How do I win this?”

Pride wants control.
Vindication.
The last word.
But God wanted obedience.
And here’s the miracle:
Rehoboam listened.

He had the power to crush.
But he chose to surrender.
He put the weapon down.
And a civil war… never happened.
Now lean in.
Because this is not just ancient history.
This is your life.

Your family.
Your relationships.
Your hidden arguments.

The messages you almost sent.
The words you almost said.
The bridges you almost burned.
Let me ask you something raw:

How many battles have you fought…
that God never authorized?

How many relationships died…
not because of truth…
but because of pride?

How many times did you say,
“I’m just being real,”

when really…
you were just being ruled by your flesh?
Scripture doesn’t stay silent here.

“What causes quarrels and what causes fights among you? Is it not this, that your passions are at war within you?”
— James 4:1

The war outside you…
is revealing the war inside you.
And that’s the deeper problem.
Because the greatest civil war is not between people.
It’s between you and God.
You want control.
God calls for surrender.
You want justice on your terms.
God offers mercy through His Son.
Here is the truth we cannot soften:
You and I were not neutral.

“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
— Romans 5:8

We were sinners.
Rebels.
Enemies.

Not misunderstood.
Not slightly off.
Lost.
And yet…
Jesus didn’t come with an army to destroy us.
He came with a cross to save us.

While we were raising weapons of pride,
He stretched out His hands in surrender.

While we demanded our way,
He said,

“Not My will, but Yours be done.”
— Luke 22:42

While we deserved judgment,
He took it.

“He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree…”
— 1 Peter 2:24
This is the Gospel:

Sin is real.
Judgment is real.
But grace is greater.

Jesus absorbed the wrath.
Paid the debt.
Opened the way.
Shemaiah stopped a physical war.
Jesus stops the eternal one.

So now the question is not:
“Are you right?”
The question is:
Are you surrendered?

Because you can win arguments…
and lose your soul.

You can be justified in your logic…
and still be far from God.

You can speak truth…
with a heart that is not submitted to Truth Himself.
Maybe today…
God is sending you your own Shemaiah moment.
Not through a prophet standing in front of you…
But through this message.
Put the weapon down.

The bitterness.
The pride.
The need to prove yourself.
Lay it down.
Repent.

Not just of what you did…
but of what is ruling your heart.
Turn to Jesus.

Not as a concept.
Not as a backup plan.
As Lord.
As Savior.
As the only One who can make peace where you’ve been making war.

“He Himself is our peace…”
— Ephesians 2:14

Not your effort.
Not your control.
Him.
And here’s the beauty:
You don’t have to clean yourself up first.
You don’t have to win first.
You don’t have to fix everything.
You just have to come.
Come with your pride.
Come with your anger.
Come with your mess.
And watch what grace does with surrendered hearts.
Some of you are one decision away…
From saving something you were about to destroy.
Don’t miss this moment.
Let it confront you.
Let it change you.
